content:
Understanding the requirements of the subclass 190 visa is the first step towards securing a successful immigration program in Australia. Each stage of the program, from eligibility and state nomination to points test and application process, plays its role in raising your chances of receiving an invitation.

This article will provide you with all the current information regarding the entire process. Everything you will require for your journey will be right here.

What Is the Subclass 190 Visa?

The Subclass 190 Visa, officially known as the Skilled Nominated Visa, is a permanent residence visa for skilled professionals who receive a nomination from an Australian state or territory government. It is intended for applicants whose occupations are in demand and who can contribute to Australia's workforce and economy.

Unlike employer-sponsored visas, the Subclass 190 Visa does not require sponsorship from an employer. Instead, applicants must first demonstrate that they possess the qualifications, skills, and work experience needed for an eligible occupation. They must also receive a nomination from an Australian state or territory before they can be invited to lodge a visa application.

Once granted, the visa allows you to:

  • Live in Australia permanently.
  • Work for any employer in Australia.
  • Study at Australian educational institutions.
  • Access Medicare, Australia's public healthcare system.
  • Sponsor eligible family members for permanent residence.
  • Travel to and from Australia in accordance with visa travel conditions.
  • Apply for Australian citizenship if you meet the eligibility requirements.

How Does the Subclass 190 Visa Work?

The application process follows a structured sequence. Before applying for the visa, candidates generally need to:

  1. Confirm that their occupation appears on an eligible skilled occupation list.
  2. Obtain a positive skills assessment from the relevant assessing authority.
  3. Meet the minimum points requirement under Australia's points-tested migration program.
  4. Submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) through SkillSelect.
  5. Receive a nomination from an Australian state or territory.
  6. Receive an Invitation to Apply (ITA) from the Department of Home Affairs.
  7. Lodge the visa application with all supporting documents.

Why Is State Nomination Important?

One of the defining features of the Subclass 190 Visa is state or territory nomination.

Australian states and territories identify occupations experiencing local shortages and nominate skilled professionals who can help fill those workforce gaps. Receiving a nomination also provides an additional five points toward your migration points score, which can improve your competitiveness during invitation rounds.

However, every state has its own nomination policies, occupation priorities, and eligibility requirements. Factors such as work experience, English proficiency, current residence, or commitment to live in the nominating state may influence whether your nomination application is successful.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The Subclass 190 Visa is suitable for skilled professionals who:

  • Want permanent residency in Australia.
  • Have an occupation that is eligible for state nomination.
  • Meet the minimum points threshold.
  • Hold a positive skills assessment.
  • Wish to build their career and settle permanently in Australia.
  • Plan to include eligible family members in their application.

For applicants whose points are not competitive enough for an independent skilled visa, state nomination can provide an additional opportunity to strengthen their profile and improve their prospects of receiving an invitation.

Key Benefits of the Subclass 190 Visa

Choosing the Subclass 190 Visa can provide long-term advantages for skilled professionals and their families. Beyond permanent residency, the visa opens access to employment opportunities, public services, and future citizenship.

Permanent Residency from Day One

One of the biggest advantages is that successful applicants become Australian permanent residents immediately after the visa is granted. There is no separate transition stage, allowing you to establish your life in Australia with long-term certainty.

Freedom to Live, Work and Study

Permanent residents can work in a wide range of occupations, pursue further education, and build their careers in Australia. While states nominate applicants based on local workforce needs, many encourage new residents to initially contribute to the nominating jurisdiction.

Access to Medicare

Eligible permanent residents can enrol in Medicare, Australia's public healthcare system, helping reduce healthcare costs and providing access to essential medical services.

Include Eligible Family Members

Applicants may include eligible family members in their visa application, enabling spouses and dependent children to enjoy many of the same permanent residency benefits.

Pathway to Australian Citizenship

After meeting the relevant residence and citizenship requirements, permanent residents may become eligible to apply for Australian citizenship, allowing them to participate fully in Australian civic life.

Greater Career Opportunities

Australia continues to experience demand for skilled professionals across industries such as healthcare, engineering, information technology, education, construction, and trades. For many applicants, the Subclass 190 Visa offers a practical route to long-term career development while contributing to Australia's skilled workforce.

Subclass 190 Visa Eligibility Criteria (2026)

Satisfying subclass 190 visa requirements is one of the most crucial aspects of immigrating to Australia through the Skilled Nominated Visa Scheme. In spite of being a direct way of gaining entry into Australia for permanent residency, candidates will need to fulfil the requirements set out by both the Australian government for the visa application and the state/territory for the nomination process.

As opposed to other forms of migration, the Subclass 190 visa operates under the points test. Some of the aspects that will be considered include age, proficiency in the English language, work experience, education, skills assessment and nomination from the state/territory in Australia. Nomination from an Australian state or territory adds 5 points to the total migration points.

Subclass 190 Visa Eligibility Criteria

Before submitting an Expression of Interest (EOI), you should ensure that you meet the core eligibility requirements established by the Australian Government.

The primary eligibility requirements include:

  • Being under the eligible age limit
  • Achieving at least Competent English
  • Obtaining a positive skills assessment
  • Having an occupation on the relevant skilled occupation list
  • Meeting the minimum points requirement
  • Receiving a nomination from an Australian state or territory
  • Receiving an Invitation to Apply (ITA)
  • Meeting health and character requirements

Age Requirement

Age plays a significant role in Australia's skilled migration program because it directly affects your points score.

To qualify for the Subclass 190 Visa, you must generally be under 45 years of age when you receive your invitation to apply. If you turn 45 before the invitation is issued, you are no longer eligible for this visa, even if you satisfy all other requirements.

English language proficiency is mandatory for the Subclass 190 Visa. At the time you receive your invitation, you must demonstrate at least Competent English through an approved English language test or another accepted method under the migration rules. Skills Assessment Requirement

A positive skills assessment confirms that your qualifications and employment history meet Australian standards for your nominated occupation.

Without a valid skills assessment, you cannot proceed with a Subclass 190 Visa application.

What Is a Skills Assessment?

A skills assessment is conducted by the designated assessing authority responsible for your occupation. The authority reviews your qualifications, professional experience, and supporting documentation before issuing its assessment.

Approved Assessing Authorities

Each occupation has its own assessing authority. Examples include organisations responsible for engineering, ICT, accounting, education, healthcare, and trade occupations. The correct authority depends on the occupation you nominate.

Validity of the Skills Assessment

For most applicants, the skills assessment must be valid when you receive your invitation. Unless the assessment specifies a different period, it generally cannot be more than three years old at the time of invitation.

Occupation List Requirement

Your nominated occupation must appear on the relevant skilled occupation list used for the Subclass 190 Visa.

Simply finding your occupation on a national list does not automatically guarantee nomination. Each Australian state or territory may publish its own eligible occupations and apply additional nomination criteria based on local workforce needs.

National Occupation Lists

The Australian Government maintains an eligible skilled occupation list for skilled migration programs.

State Occupation Lists

States and territories may prioritise occupations experiencing local shortages. These lists are reviewed periodically, so applicants should always confirm current requirements before lodging an EOI.

Minimum Points Requirement

The Subclass 190 Visa is points-tested.

To be eligible, you must have at least 65 points at the time of invitation. However, the minimum threshold does not guarantee that you will receive an invitation. In many occupations and states, invited applicants have significantly higher scores due to competition. State nomination contributes an additional 5 points to your total.

Your overall score may be calculated from factors such as:

  • Age
  • English language ability
  • Skilled employment
  • Educational qualifications
  • Australian study
  • Professional Year
  • Partner skills
  • Community language credentials
  • State nomination

Health Requirement

Australia requires permanent visa applicants to meet specific health standards.

You and any eligible family members included in your application may need to complete medical examinations through approved panel physicians. The purpose is to ensure applicants satisfy Australia's public health requirements.

Character Requirement

Applicants aged 16 years or older generally need to satisfy Australia's character requirements.

This commonly involves providing police clearance certificates from countries where you have lived for the required period, along with any additional information requested during visa processing.

State Nomination Requirement

State nomination is one of the defining features of the Subclass 190 Visa.

Unlike the Skilled Independent Visa (Subclass 189), you must first receive a nomination from an Australian state or territory government before you can receive an invitation to apply.

Each state sets its own nomination criteria, which may include:

  • Occupation demand
  • Work experience
  • English proficiency
  • Current residence
  • Employment history
  • Commitment to contribute to the state's economy

Receiving a nomination not only satisfies a key visa requirement but also adds 5 points to your migration score.

Invitation to Apply (ITA)

Meeting all eligibility criteria does not automatically result in a visa application.

The general sequence is:

  1. Confirm your eligibility.
  2. Obtain a positive skills assessment.
  3. Submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) through SkillSelect.
  4. Apply for state or territory nomination (where applicable).
  5. Receive an Invitation to Apply (ITA).
  6. Lodge your Subclass 190 Visa application with supporting documentation. (Immigration and Citizenship Website)

Receiving an invitation is the point at which you can formally submit your permanent visa application to the Australian Government.

Knowledge of how the Subclass 190 Visa point test functions may help you to create a strong application profile. The following part describes the details of each point’s criterion, the way your points are counted, and gives useful recommendations.

  • Meet the minimum eligibility score.
  • Receive a nomination from an Australian state or territory.
  • Receive an Invitation to Apply (ITA).
  • Provide evidence supporting every point claimed in your EOI.

State Nomination Explained for the Subclass 190 Visa (2026)

State nomination is one of the most important aspects of the subclass 190 visa application process. Unlike independent skilled migration pathways, the Skilled Nominated Visa requires you to receive an official nomination from an Australian state or territory before you can be invited to apply for permanent residency.

For skilled professionals planning to immigrate to Australia, understanding how state nomination works can significantly improve the chances of receiving an invitation. Every Australian state and territory identifies occupations facing local skill shortages and nominates applicants who can contribute to its economy and workforce. As a result, each jurisdiction has its own occupation priorities, eligibility criteria, and selection process.

What Is State Nomination?

State nomination is a process where an Australian state or territory government supports your application for a Subclass 190 Visa after assessing that your skills match its labour market needs.

Unlike employer-sponsored visas, the nomination comes from a government authority rather than an employer. Once nominated, you receive 5 additional migration points, which are added to your points-tested score and may improve your chances of receiving an Invitation to Apply (ITA).

Why Is State Nomination Important?

Receiving a state nomination offers several advantages:

  • Adds 5 bonus points to your migration score.
  • Increases your competitiveness in the SkillSelect invitation process.
  • Supports Australia's workforce needs in specific industries.
  • Provides a direct pathway to Australia PR.
  • Opens opportunities for applicants whose points may not be high enough for an independent skilled visa.

How Australian States Select Applicants

Each state and territory manages its own nomination program independently.

Although all applicants must satisfy the Department of Home Affairs' subclass 190 visa requirements, states often apply additional selection criteria based on local labour market demand.

Common factors considered include:

  • Occupation demand within the state.
  • English language proficiency.
  • Skilled work experience.
  • Educational qualifications.
  • Current employment.
  • Residency status (onshore or offshore).
  • Commitment to live and work in the nominating state.
  • Overall competitiveness of the applicant's profile.

Because these priorities can change throughout the program year, applicants should review the latest state-specific requirements before lodging a nomination application.

Registration of Interest (ROI)

Some Australian states require applicants to submit a Registration of Interest (ROI) before they can apply for nomination.

An ROI is not a visa application or a nomination application. Instead, it allows the state government to assess your profile and determine whether you should be invited to apply for nomination.

For example, Victoria operates an ROI system where applicants first submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) through SkillSelect and then lodge an ROI through the state's migration portal. Only selected applicants are invited to proceed with a nomination application.

State Nomination Process

Although each jurisdiction has its own procedures, the general process is similar across Australia.

Step 1: Confirm Your Eligibility

Before applying, ensure you satisfy both:

  • Department of Home Affairs eligibility requirements.
  • State or territory nomination criteria.

Step 2: Submit an Expression of Interest (EOI)

Create or update your EOI through SkillSelect.

Your EOI includes information such as:

  • Age
  • Education
  • Work experience
  • English proficiency
  • Skills assessment
  • Preferred states

Step 3: Apply for State Nomination (or ROI)

Depending on the jurisdiction, you may need to:

  • Submit an ROI.
  • Lodge a nomination application directly.
  • Wait for the state to invite eligible applicants.

Step 4: Receive State Nomination

If your application is successful, the state will nominate you through SkillSelect.

You will automatically receive an additional 5 migration points.

Step 5: Receive an Invitation to Apply (ITA)

After nomination, the Department of Home Affairs may issue an Invitation to Apply.

You generally have 60 days from the invitation date to lodge your visa application.

State-Specific Eligibility Overview

Although the visa framework is national, every Australian state and territory sets its own nomination priorities. Below is a high-level overview.

Selecting the most suitable state is often just as important as meeting the basic subclass 190 visa requirements.

A strategic state selection can significantly improve your prospects of obtaining Australia PR, especially in competitive occupations.

Common Reasons State Nomination Applications Are Unsuccessful

Although eligibility is important, nomination is never guaranteed.

  • Insufficient evidence supporting claims.
  • Failure to meet state-specific criteria.
  • Incorrect information in the EOI.
  • Expired skills assessment or English test.
  • Not responding to requests for additional information within the required timeframe.

Skilled Occupation Lists for the Subclass 190 Visa (2026)

Meeting the criteria for the subclass 190 visa is one of the most important things when immigrating to Australia under the Skilled Nominated Visa Scheme. Despite the fact that this is a clear way of entering Australia for permanent residence, there will be certain requirements to be met in relation to the visa application and the nomination process, both from the Australian government and the state/territory.

Unlike any other type of migration, the Subclass 190 visa will be considered on the basis of the points test. Among those things that will be taken into account are age, English language skills, work experience, education, skills assessment, and nomination from the state/territory in Australia.

What Is the Skilled Occupation List?

Australia uses Skilled Occupation Lists to identify professions experiencing workforce shortages across different industries.

These lists help the Australian Government and state and territory governments select skilled professionals who can contribute to economic growth and address labour market gaps.

For the Subclass 190 Visa, your nominated occupation must:

  • Be eligible under the relevant skilled occupation framework.
  • Be assessed by the appropriate skills assessing authority.
  • Meet your chosen state's nomination requirements.
  • Match your qualifications and skilled work experience.

How Occupation Lists Work

Many applicants assume that Australia has one single occupation list. In reality, there are multiple occupation lists that determine eligibility for different skilled migration pathways.

For the Subclass 190 Visa, the most relevant lists include:

  • Medium and Long-term Strategic Skills List (MLTSSL)
  • Short-term Skilled Occupation List (STSOL)

Some states also publish their own nomination lists or priority occupation lists based on local workforce shortages.

Medium and Long-term Strategic Skills List (MLTSSL)

The MLTSSL contains occupations considered important to Australia's long-term economic development.

Professionals whose occupations appear on this list generally have access to several skilled migration pathways, including:

  • Subclass 189 Visa
  • Subclass 190 Visa
  • Subclass 491 Visa

Examples include many engineering, healthcare, ICT, education, and skilled trade occupations.

Short-term Skilled Occupation List (STSOL)

The STSOL includes occupations that address more immediate workforce needs.

Many STSOL occupations are eligible for the Subclass 190 Visa, provided the relevant Australian state or territory includes them in its nomination program.

Eligibility may differ between states, so applicants should always check the latest nomination criteria before submitting an application.

State Occupation Lists

Every Australian state and territory has the flexibility to prioritise occupations based on its own labour market requirements.

For example:

  • A profession may be open for nomination in one state but unavailable in another.
  • Some states prioritise healthcare and engineering.
  • Others may focus on construction, education, agriculture, or regional development.

Because nomination programs change throughout the migration year, applicants should verify the current occupation list before lodging an Expression of Interest (EOI).

One of the most vital things when it comes to the process of visa application under subclass 190 visa is to ensure your documentation is perfect. Each of the claims that you have made in your Expression of Interest (EOI) regarding your age, education, English language proficiency, work experience, and qualifications should be backed up by documentary proof whenever you apply for the visa.

This section explains the key documents you should prepare before applying for the Subclass 190 Visa and provides practical tips to help you organise your application efficiently.

Identity Documents

Most applicants will need:

  • Valid passport
  • Recent passport-sized photograph (if requested)
  • National identity card (if applicable)
  • Birth certificate (where available)

If your name has changed, include official evidence such as:

  • Legal name change certificate
  • Government-issued name change records

Passport Requirements

A valid passport is essential throughout the application process.

Your application should include:

  • Bio-data page
  • Passport number
  • Issue date
  • Expiry date
  • Personal details page

If your passport expires soon, renewing it before lodging your visa application may help avoid unnecessary administrative updates during processing.

Educational Documents

Educational qualifications support both your skills assessment and your migration points claim.

Required Educational Documents

Depending on your qualifications, prepare:

  • Degree certificates
  • Diploma certificates
  • Trade qualification certificates
  • Academic transcripts
  • Completion letters
  • Professional certifications (where relevant)

Applicants claiming education points must ensure that their qualifications are recognised for migration purposes and supported by the appropriate evidence.

Employment Documents

Work experience often contributes a significant number of points toward the Subclass 190 Visa.

Because employment claims are closely examined, applicants should provide comprehensive supporting evidence.

Employment Reference Letters

Reference letters should ideally include:

  • Company letterhead
  • Job title
  • Employment dates
  • Working hours

Supporting Employment Evidence

Skills Assessment Documents

You should include:

  • Reference number
  • Assessment date
  • Supporting assessment documents (if applicable)

State Nomination Documents

Applicants nominated by an Australian state or territory should retain evidence of their nomination.

Depending on the jurisdiction, this may include:

  • Nomination approval notification
  • Invitation email
  • Registration of Interest (ROI) outcome (where applicable)

Although much of the nomination process is handled electronically, keeping copies of these records is recommended.

Police Clearance Certificates

Australia requires most applicants aged 16 years or older to satisfy character requirements.

You may need:

  • Joint bank account statements
  • Joint lease agreements
  • Utility bills in both names
  • Photographs
  • Evidence of shared financial commitments

  • Passports

Step-by-Step Subclass 190 Visa Application Process (2026)

Applying for the subclass 190 visa involves more than simply submitting an application. It is a structured process that begins with confirming your eligibility and ends with receiving a permanent residency decision from the Australian Government.

For professionals planning to immigrate to Australia, following the correct sequence is essential. Missing a step, claiming incorrect points, or submitting incomplete documentation can delay processing or affect your application outcome.

This section provides a practical, step-by-step guide to help you understand each stage of the Australia immigration process for the Skilled Nominated Visa. The overall process is managed through SkillSelect and ImmiAccount, with state or territory nomination playing a central role.

Overview of the Subclass 190 Visa Application Process

The application journey generally follows these stages:

  1. Check your eligibility.
  2. Take an approved English language test.
  3. Obtain a positive skills assessment.
  4. Calculate your migration points.
  5. Submit an Expression of Interest (EOI).
  6. Apply for state or territory nomination.
  7. Receive an Invitation to Apply (ITA).
  8. Lodge your visa application.
  9. Complete health and character requirements.
  10. Wait for the visa decision and prepare for your move to Australia.

Step 1: Check Your Eligibility

Before investing time and money in the process, confirm that you meet the core subclass 190 visa requirements.

At a minimum, you should:

  • Be under 45 years of age when invited.
  • Have an eligible occupation.
  • Obtain a suitable skills assessment.
  • Meet the minimum English language requirement.
  • Score at least 65 migration points.
  • Be eligible for nomination by an Australian state or territory.
  • Meet health and character requirements.

Create an Eligibility Checklist

Before moving forward, ask yourself:

  • Is my occupation eligible?
  • Can I obtain a positive skills assessment?
  • Do I have sufficient work experience?
  • Have I calculated my migration points correctly?
  • Which Australian state best suits my profile?

Starting with a realistic assessment can help you avoid unnecessary delays later in the process.

Step 2: Complete an English Language Test

English language proficiency is mandatory for the Subclass 190 Visa.

Choose one of the approved English language tests, such as:

  • IELTS
  • PTE Academic
  • TOEFL iBT
  • Cambridge C1 Advanced
  • OET (for eligible healthcare professionals)

A higher English score can increase your migration points and may also improve your competitiveness for state nomination.

Aim Higher Than the Minimum

Although Competent English satisfies the basic requirement, many applicants benefit from achieving Proficient or Superior English because it can significantly increase their overall points score.

Step 3: Obtain a Positive Skills Assessment

A suitable skills assessment is mandatory before submitting your EOI.

Your nominated occupation determines which assessing authority evaluates your qualifications and employment experience.

Skills Assessment Checklist

Prepare:

  • Educational qualifications
  • Academic transcripts
  • Employment reference letters
  • Payslips or tax documents (where applicable)
  • Identity documents
  • Professional licences (if required)

The assessing authority will determine whether your qualifications and work experience meet Australian standards for your nominated occupation.

Step 4: Calculate Your Migration Points

Before submitting an Expression of Interest, calculate your migration score carefully.

 

Points may be awarded for:

  • Age
  • English language ability
  • Skilled work experience
  • Educational qualifications
  • Australian study
  • Professional Year
  • Partner skills
  • Credentialled community language
  • Regional study
  • State nomination

Verify Every Point Claimed

Every point claimed in your EOI must later be supported by documentary evidence.

Incorrect claims can affect the outcome of your application.

Step 5: Submit an Expression of Interest (EOI)

Once your eligibility has been confirmed, submit your Expression of Interest (EOI) through SkillSelect.

An EOI is not a visa application. It is an online profile that provides information about your qualifications, skills, work experience, English ability, and migration points.

Importantly:

  • There is no government fee to submit an EOI.
  • Your EOI can be lodged while you are inside or outside Australia.
  • You should update your EOI if your circumstances change, such as gaining more work experience or improving your English score.

Information Included in Your EOI

Your EOI generally contains:

  • Personal details
  • Occupation
  • Skills assessment information
  • English test results
  • Employment history
  • Educational qualifications
  • Migration points
  • Preferred state or territory

Step 6: Apply for State or Territory Nomination

After submitting your EOI, the next step is obtaining state nomination.

Depending on your chosen jurisdiction, you may need to:

  • Submit a Registration of Interest (ROI).
  • Lodge a separate nomination application.
  • Wait for the state to invite eligible applicants.

Each Australian state and territory applies its own nomination criteria and occupation priorities. Receiving a nomination adds 5 points to your migration score.

Improve Your Nomination Prospects

You may strengthen your application by:

  • Choosing a state where your occupation is in demand.
  • Keeping your EOI current.
  • Demonstrating relevant work experience.
  • Achieving a stronger English score.

Step 7: Receive an Invitation to Apply (ITA)

If you are nominated by a state or territory and selected through SkillSelect, the Department of Home Affairs may issue an Invitation to Apply (ITA).

Receiving an ITA allows you to submit your permanent visa application.

Time Limit After Receiving an Invitation

Once invited, you generally have 60 calendar days to lodge your Subclass 190 Visa application. Missing this deadline means you cannot use that invitation and will need to wait for another opportunity.

Step 8: Lodge Your Visa Application

After receiving your invitation, submit your application online through ImmiAccount.

At this stage, you should:

  • Upload all required supporting documents.
  • Ensure the information matches your EOI.
  • Pay the applicable visa application charge.
  • Keep a record of your Transaction Reference Number (TRN).

Double-Check Before Submission

Before clicking "Submit," review:

  • Passport details
  • Skills assessment
  • English test results
  • Employment evidence
  • Educational documents
  • Family member information

Small errors at this stage can result in requests for additional information and extend processing times.

Step 9: Complete Health and Character Requirements

After lodging your application, you may be asked to complete:

Health Examinations

Medical examinations are carried out through approved panel physicians.

The required tests depend on factors such as:

  • Age
  • Medical history
  • Country of residence
  • Individual circumstances

Character Assessment

Applicants aged 16 years or older are generally required to provide police clearance certificates from eligible countries where they have lived for the required period.

Step 10: Wait for Your Visa Decision

Once all requirements have been met, the Department of Home Affairs will assess your application.

During this stage, the Department may:

  • Request additional documents.
  • Seek clarification regarding the information submitted.
  • Conduct verification checks.
  • Finalise health and character assessments.

You can monitor the status of your application through your ImmiAccount. The Department generally does not provide status updates while an application is still within its standard processing timeframe.

What Happens After Your Visa Is Granted?

If your application is approved, you will receive a written visa grant notification containing:

  • Visa grant number
  • Visa commencement details
  • Travel facility information
  • Any applicable visa conditions

As a permanent resident, you can:

  • Live and work in Australia permanently.
  • Study in Australia.
  • Enrol in Medicare if eligible.
  • Sponsor eligible relatives.
  • Work towards Australian citizenship if you meet the legal requirements.

Common Mistakes to Avoid During the Application Process

  • Lodging an outdated or inaccurate EOI.
  • Submitting expired English test results or skills assessments.
  • Uploading incomplete employment documents.
  • Missing the 60-day deadline after receiving an ITA.
  • Failing to notify the Department if your circumstances change after applying.

While meeting the eligibility criteria is important, applicants should also plan their budget and prepare for the time required to complete each stage of the process.

Likewise, your overall expenses extend beyond the government visa application charge and may include costs for skills assessments, English tests, medical examinations, police clearances, and document translations.

Is the Subclass 190 Visa Worth the Investment?

For many skilled professionals seeking an Australia PR, the Subclass 190 Visa offers long-term value despite the upfront costs.

Successful applicants receive permanent residency, allowing them to:

  • Live and work in Australia indefinitely.
  • Study in Australia.
  • Access Medicare (if eligible).
  • Sponsor eligible family members.
  • Travel to and from Australia in accordance with the visa's travel facility.
  • Become eligible to apply for Australian citizenship if they meet the legal requirements.

Viewed as a long-term investment, careful financial planning and thorough preparation can make the application process more manageable and improve your chances of a smooth outcome.

Benefits of the Subclass 190 Visa (2026)

The subclass 190 visa is one of Australia's most popular skilled migration pathways because it grants permanent residency (PR) from the day your visa is approved. Unlike temporary work visas, it allows eligible skilled professionals and their families to establish long-term careers and lives in Australia.

For individuals planning to immigrate to Australia, the Skilled Nominated Visa offers far more than the ability to work. It provides access to healthcare, education, family sponsorship opportunities, international travel, and a future pathway to Australian citizenship. While applicants are nominated by a state or territory government, the visa itself is a permanent residence visa issued by the Australian Government.

Why Choose the Subclass 190 Visa?

The Subclass 190 Visa combines the security of permanent residency with the advantage of state nomination.

Some of its key benefits include:

  • Permanent resident status from the date of visa grant.
  • Ability to live, work, and study in Australia.
  • Access to Australia's public healthcare system (if eligible).
  • Ability to include eligible family members.
  • Opportunity to sponsor eligible relatives.
  • Pathway to Australian citizenship, subject to meeting legal requirements.
  • An International travel facility is attached to the visa.

Permanent Residency from Day One

One of the biggest advantages of the subclass 190 visa is that it is a permanent residence visa.

Unlike provisional or temporary visas, successful applicants become Australian permanent residents immediately after the visa is granted.

Permanent residency allows you to:

  • Live in Australia indefinitely.
  • Work without employer restrictions.
  • Study at Australian educational institutions.
  • Build a long-term career.
  • Establish your family in Australia.

Live and Work in Australia

The Subclass 190 Visa allows you to accept employment in Australia without needing employer sponsorship.

You may:

  • Work full-time or part-time.
  • Change employers.
  • Start your own business.
  • Pursue self-employment.
  • Work across a wide range of industries.

Although applicants are nominated by a particular state or territory, they are generally expected to honour their commitment to live and work in the nominating jurisdiction, particularly during the initial settlement period. This expectation supports the purpose of state nomination.

Study Opportunities

Permanent residents can access Australia's education system and pursue further qualifications.

Many visa holders choose to:

  • Complete postgraduate studies.
  • Obtain Australian professional certifications.
  • Improve career prospects through higher education.
  • Enrol in vocational education and training programs.

Studying in Australia can also help skilled professionals expand their employment opportunities.

Access to Medicare

Eligible permanent residents can enrol in Medicare, Australia's public healthcare system.

Depending on eligibility, Medicare may provide access to:

  • Public hospital services.
  • Medical consultations.
  • Diagnostic services.
  • Prescription medicine subsidies under eligible programs.

Access to Medicare is one of the major advantages of obtaining Australia PR through the Skilled Nominated Visa.

Include Eligible Family Members

The Subclass 190 Visa allows eligible family members to be included in the same visa application.

Depending on your circumstances, this may include:

  • Your spouse or de facto partner.
  • Dependent children.
  • Certain dependent relatives were permitted under Australian migration law.

Including eligible family members enables the entire family to relocate together and enjoy the benefits of permanent residency.

Sponsor Eligible Relatives

After becoming a permanent resident, you may be able to sponsor eligible relatives for certain Australian visas, provided you meet the applicable sponsorship requirements.

Family sponsorship options are governed by Australian migration legislation and vary depending on the visa category.

Pathway to Australian Citizenship

For many applicants, the Subclass 190 Visa serves as a long-term pathway towards Australian citizenship.

Subject to meeting all legal requirements, including residence and character requirements, permanent residents may become eligible to apply for Australian citizenship in the future.

Australian citizenship offers additional benefits such as:

  • An Australian passport.
  • The right to vote in eligible elections.
  • Eligibility for certain government positions.
  • Full participation in Australian civic life.

Travel In and Out of Australia

The Subclass 190 Visa includes a travel facility that allows visa holders to leave and re-enter Australia for a specified period from the date of visa grant.

If you wish to travel after the travel facility expires while retaining your permanent resident status, you may need to apply for a Resident Return Visa (RRV), provided you meet the relevant requirements.

Employment Flexibility

Unlike employer-sponsored visas, the Subclass 190 Visa provides greater flexibility in your career.

You can:

  • Change employers.
  • Change occupations (subject to professional licensing where applicable).
  • Accept promotions.
  • Start your own company.
  • Pursue freelance or consulting opportunities where permitted by Australian law.

This flexibility allows skilled migrants to adapt as their careers evolve.

Long-Term Career Growth

Australia continues to experience demand across sectors such as:

  • Healthcare
  • Information Technology
  • Engineering
  • Construction
  • Education
  • Skilled Trades

Permanent residency enables you to compete for long-term employment opportunities without requiring ongoing employer sponsorship, making career progression more straightforward.

Quality of Life

Many skilled migrants choose Australia because of its high standard of living.

Some of the lifestyle advantages include:

  • Modern infrastructure.
  • High-quality healthcare.
  • Internationally recognised education system.
  • Safe and multicultural communities.
  • Strong employment opportunities.
  • Work-life balance.
  • Diverse natural landscapes and an outdoor lifestyle.

These factors make Australia an attractive destination for professionals and families planning a long-term future.

Common Reasons for Subclass 190 Visa Refusal & How to Avoid Them (2026)

Applying for the subclass 190 visa requires careful preparation, accurate documentation, and strict compliance with Australia's migration laws. Although many applicants successfully obtain an Australia PR visa, refusals can occur when eligibility requirements are not met or when supporting evidence is insufficient.

A refusal does not necessarily mean an applicant lacks qualifications or experience. In many cases, applications are refused because of avoidable mistakes, such as incorrect points claims, incomplete documentation, expired assessments, or inconsistencies between the Expression of Interest (EOI) and the visa application.

Understanding the most common refusal reasons can help you prepare a stronger application and improve your chances of successfully immigrating to Australia. The Department of Home Affairs assesses every application against the Migration Act, Migration Regulations, and the visa criteria that apply to the Subclass 190 Visa.

Can a Subclass 190 Visa Be Refused?

Yes, meeting the minimum subclass 190 visa requirements or receiving state nomination does not guarantee visa approval.

The Department of Home Affairs independently assesses every application to determine whether the applicant satisfies all legislative requirements before granting permanent residency. If the criteria are not met, the visa may be refused.

Common Reasons for Subclass 190 Visa Refusal

Below are some of the most common reasons applications are refused.

  1. Incorrect Migration Points Claims

One of the leading reasons for refusal is claiming points that cannot be supported with evidence.

Examples include:

  • Incorrect work experience calculations.
  • Claiming educational qualifications that are not recognised.
  • Claiming partner points without meeting the eligibility criteria.
  • Claiming English language points not supported by valid test results.

The Department verifies every point claimed in your EOI. If you cannot provide acceptable evidence, your application may be refused.

How to Avoid This

  • Calculate your points carefully.
  • Keep supporting evidence for every claim.
  • Update your EOI if your circumstances change.
  • Avoid estimating work experience or qualifications.

  1. Invalid or Expired Skills Assessment

A positive skills assessment is a mandatory requirement for the Subclass 190 Visa.

Applications may be refused if:

  • The assessment has expired.
  • The occupation does not match the EOI.
  • The assessing authority withdraws or does not recognise the assessment.
  • The applicant fails to meet the assessment requirements.

How to Avoid This

  • Confirm the validity period of your assessment.
  • Ensure your nominated occupation is correct.
  • Keep all assessment documents ready before lodging your application.

  1. English Language Requirements Not Met

Applicants must satisfy the required English language standard.

Problems commonly arise when:

  • Test results expire before the relevant stage of the application.
  • The claimed English level differs from the official score report.
  • Incorrect test details are entered into the EOI.

How to Avoid This

  • Check your test validity carefully.
  • Upload the official score report.
  • Retake the test if necessary before lodging your application.

  1. Incomplete or Incorrect Documentation

Missing documents can delay processing and, in some circumstances, lead to refusal.

Common examples include:

  • Missing employment references.
  • Missing educational certificates.
  • Incomplete passport pages.
  • Missing translations.
  • Inadequate identity documents.

How to Avoid This

Prepare all supporting documents well before receiving your Invitation to Apply (ITA).

  1. False or Misleading Information

Providing false, altered, forged, or misleading information is one of the most serious reasons a visa may be refused.

Examples include:

  • Fake employment letters.
  • Altered bank statements.
  • Forged educational qualifications.
  • Incorrect employment history.
  • Misrepresented relationship information.

The Department may verify documents directly with employers, universities, assessing authorities, and government agencies. Providing bogus documents or materially false information can lead not only to refusal but also to serious legal consequences and restrictions on future visa applications.

How to Avoid This

  • Submit only genuine documents.
  • Review every document before uploading.
  • Ensure your migration professional, if you use one, submits accurate information.
  • Immediately correct any genuine mistakes if identified.

  1. Health Requirements Not Met

All applicants must satisfy Australia's health requirements.

Applications may be affected if:

  • Required medical examinations have not been completed.
  • Additional medical information is requested but not provided.
  • The applicant does not satisfy the applicable health criteria.

How to Avoid This

  • Attend medical examinations promptly.
  • Follow instructions from the Department.
  • Submit the requested medical information within the specified timeframe.

  1. Character Requirements Not Met

Applicants aged 16 years or older generally need to satisfy Australia's character requirements.

Potential issues include:

  • Serious criminal convictions.
  • Failure to disclose criminal history.
  • Missing police clearance certificates.
  • Providing inaccurate information about previous offences.

How to Avoid This

  • Disclose all relevant information honestly.
  • Obtain police certificates from every required country.
  • Respond fully to any Department requests.

  1. Problems with State Nomination

Although you may initially receive a nomination, issues can still arise if:

  • Information in your nomination application differs from your EOI.
  • State nomination is withdrawn before the visa grant.
  • You no longer meet the state's nomination criteria.

How to Avoid This

  • Keep your EOI consistent with your nomination application.
  • Notify the state authority if your circumstances change.
  • Continue meeting nomination obligations throughout the application process.

  1. Failure to Meet Time Limits

Applicants must comply with important deadlines.

Examples include:

  • Not lodging the visa application within 60 days of receiving the Invitation to Apply.
  • Missing requests for additional information.
  • Failing to complete health examinations on time.

How to Avoid This

  • Monitor your ImmiAccount regularly.
  • Respond to Department requests promptly.
  • Keep copies of all submitted documents.

  1. Changes in Personal Circumstances

Applicants must notify the Department if important circumstances change after lodging the application.

Examples include:

  • Marriage or divorce.
  • Birth of a child.
  • Passport renewal.
  • Change of residential address.
  • Change of email or contact details.

Failing to update this information may affect visa processing or create inconsistencies in your application.

What Happens If Your Visa Is Refused?

If your application is refused, the Department will provide a written decision explaining:

  • The reason for refusal.
  • The legislative provisions applied.
  • Whether you have review rights.
  • Any applicable time limits for seeking a review?

The visa application charge is generally not refunded if your application is refused. 

Practical Tips to Reduce the Risk of Refusal

To strengthen your Subclass 190 Visa application:

  • Verify your migration points before submitting your EOI.
  • Obtain a valid skills assessment.
  • Ensure your English test remains valid.
  • Prepare complete employment evidence.
  • Submit only genuine and verifiable documents.
  • Keep your passport current.
  • Respond quickly to Department requests.
  • Review every document carefully before lodging your application.
  • Inform the Department promptly if your personal circumstances change.

If you're planning to immigrate to Australia through the Subclass 190 Visa, taking the right steps from the beginning can make the process smoother and more efficient.

Conclusion 

Applying for the subclass 190 visa can seem complex, especially if it is your first time navigating Australia's skilled migration system. Throughout this guide, we have covered the eligibility criteria, points test, state nomination, occupation lists, required documents, application process, processing times, benefits, and common reasons for refusal.

faqs.q: What is the Subclass 190 Visa?
faqs.a: The Subclass 190 Visa, also known as the Skilled Nominated Visa, is a points-tested permanent residence visa for skilled workers who are nominated by an Australian state or territory government. Successful applicants receive permanent residency and can live, work, and study in Australia.

faqs.q: Is the Subclass 190 Visa Permanent?
faqs.a: Yes, the Subclass 190 Visa is a permanent visa, meaning successful applicants become Australian permanent residents from the date the visa is granted.

faqs.q: What Is the Minimum Points Requirement?
faqs.a: You must have at least 65 points to be eligible to receive an invitation. However, 65 points is only the minimum eligibility threshold. Depending on your occupation and the state nomination program, competitive applicants often require higher scores.

faqs.q: Is State Nomination Mandatory?
faqs.a: Yes. Unlike the Skilled Independent Visa (Subclass 189), the Subclass 190 Visa requires nomination by an Australian state or territory before you can receive an Invitation to Apply (ITA).

faqs.q: Can I Include My Family?
faqs.a:
Yes. You can generally include eligible family members, such as:
Your spouse or de facto partner.
Dependent children.
Other eligible dependents were permitted under Australian migration law.

faqs.q: Do I Need a Job Offer?
faqs.a: No. A job offer is not a mandatory requirement for the Subclass 190 Visa. However, some states may give preference to applicants with employment in their jurisdiction or occupations experiencing strong demand.

faqs.q: Can I Apply from Outside Australia?
faqs.a: Yes. You can submit your Expression of Interest (EOI) and apply for the Subclass 190 Visa, whether you are inside or outside Australia, provided you meet the eligibility requirements.

faqs.q: Do I Need a Skills Assessment?
faqs.a: Yes. A positive skills assessment from the appropriate assessing authority is mandatory before you can be invited to apply for the visa.

faqs.q: How Long Is My EOI Valid?
faqs.a: An Expression of Interest (EOI) generally remains valid in SkillSelect for up to two years, unless you withdraw it or receive an invitation. You should keep your EOI updated if your circumstances change, such as gaining additional work experience or improving your English score.

faqs.q: Can My Visa Be Refused Even After State Nomination?
faqs.a: Yes. Receiving a state nomination does not guarantee visa approval. The Department of Home Affairs independently assesses every application against the legal visa criteria.

The following article will help you learn more about the points-based Australia Subclass 491 Visa.

What Is the Australia Subclass 491 Visa?

The Subclass 491 Skilled Visa is a temporary migration visa that allows eligible workers to migrate to Australia’s designated regional areas and reside there for four years. This visa aids regional development in that it helps governments of the states and territories of Australia fill skill shortages while providing a pathway for permanent residency to the eligible migrants.

As compared to other employer-sponsored visas, this visa is all about skills and points scores. In order to apply for this visa, you must have either been nominated by the government of a particular state or territory of Australia or been sponsored by an eligible family member in the designated regional area of Australia.

Who Should Consider the Subclass 491 Visa?

The visa may be suitable for:

  • Skilled professionals seeking to immigrate to Australia.
  • Applicants who meet the skilled migration points threshold.
  • Individuals whose occupation appears on an eligible skilled occupation list.
  • Applicants willing to live and work in designated regional Australia.
  • Families looking for a structured pathway towards Australian permanent residency.

While most of the temporary visas are restrictive in nature, the Subclass 491 Visa Australia is flexible in nature.

Live and Work in Regional Australia

Among other advantages that come with the subclass 491 visa, one of the greatest benefits is the possibility to reside and work in Australia’s regional areas. Such areas provide ample employment prospects, good infrastructure, a low cost of living compared to many large cities, and a high standard of living.

Depending on your chosen profession and state nomination criteria, you can start building your career in the area where there are chronic labor shortages.

Five-Year Visa Validity

The Subclass 491 Visa allows eligible applicants to stay in Australia for up to five years.

During this period you can:

  • Live in designated regional Australia.
  • Work for eligible employers.
  • Study in Australia.
  • Travel internationally while your visa remains valid.

This longer validity provides time to establish yourself professionally and work toward meeting the requirements for permanent residence. 

Include Eligible Family Members

Your application may include eligible members of your family, such as:

  • Spouse or de facto partner.
  • Dependent children.
  • Other eligible dependent family members where permitted.

Including your family from the beginning allows everyone to relocate together and enjoy the benefits of living in regional Australia.

Pathway Towards Permanent Residency

Although the Subclass 491 Visa Australia is a provisional visa, it can create an opportunity to apply for permanent residence through the Subclass 191 Permanent Residence (Skilled Regional) Visa, provided you satisfy the applicable eligibility requirements.

Access to Regional Career Opportunities

Regional Australia continues to experience demand for skilled workers across many industries, including:

  • Information Technology
  • Engineering
  • Healthcare
  • Education
  • Construction
  • Hospitality
  • Agriculture
  • Skilled Trades

This demand creates valuable opportunities for qualified professionals planning to immigrate to Australia.

Multiple Travel Rights

As a Subclass 491 visa holder, you can travel in and out of Australia multiple times while your visa remains valid, making it easier to maintain personal and professional commitments overseas.

Who Can Apply for the Subclass 491 Visa?

The subclass 491 visa is intended for skilled workers who can contribute to Australia's regional workforce. Before submitting an Expression of Interest (EOI), you should ensure you satisfy the core eligibility requirements established by the Australian Government.

Age Requirement

At the time you receive your invitation to apply, you must generally be under 45 years of age.

Applicants who have already turned 45 before receiving an invitation are generally not eligible under this visa category.

Occupation Requirement

Your nominated occupation must appear on the relevant skilled occupation list applicable to the Subclass 491 visa.

The occupation selected should accurately reflect your qualifications, skills, and work experience.

Skills Assessment

You must obtain a positive skills assessment from the relevant assessing authority for your nominated occupation before applying.

The assessment confirms that your qualifications and experience meet Australian standards for your profession. In most cases, the assessment must still be valid when you receive your invitation.

State Nomination or Eligible Relative Sponsorship

To apply for the Subclass 491 Visa Australia, you must receive either:

  • Nomination from an Australian state or territory government, or
  • Sponsorship from an eligible relative living in a designated regional area of Australia.

Without one of these, you cannot proceed with a Subclass 491 application.

Expression of Interest (EOI)

Before lodging a visa application, applicants must submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) through SkillSelect.

Your EOI provides information about your:

  • Age
  • Education
  • Employment history
  • English language ability
  • Skills assessment
  • Claimed migration points

You can apply only after receiving an invitation from the Department of Home Affairs.

English Language Requirement

Applicants must demonstrate at least Competent English at the time of invitation.

Higher English proficiency may increase your points score and improve your competitiveness for invitations. 

Points Test

The Subclass 491 Visa Australia is a points-tested visa.

You must achieve at least 65 points to be eligible for consideration. However, depending on your occupation and nomination pathway, invited applicants may need higher scores because invitations are competitive.

Health and Character Requirements

Applicants and included family members must satisfy Australia's health and character requirements.

This generally involves:

  • Medical examinations.
  • Police clearance certificates.
  • Additional documents if requested by the Department of Home Affairs.

Australia 491 Visa Eligibility Checklist

Before starting your application, use the checklist below to determine whether you meet the basic requirements.

If you answer "Yes" to each point above, you may be in a strong position to continue your subclass 491 visa application. Final eligibility will always depend on your individual circumstances and current Australian Government requirements.

Australia Skilled Migration Points Test Explained

The skilled migration policy in Australia applies the points system in order to evaluate candidates objectively. The total number of points will depend on a range of elements including age, English language proficiency, education level, skilled employment, among others.

It should be noted that the minimum point score needed in order to be considered for the Subclass 491 Visa Australia is 65 points; however, a high score will increase your chances of being invited.

Key Factors That Influence Your Points

The migration points test may award points for:

  • Age.
  • English language proficiency.
  • Overseas skilled employment.
  • Australian skilled employment.
  • Educational qualifications.
  • Australian study requirement.
  • Specialist education qualifications.
  • Study in regional Australia.
  • Credentialled community language.
  • Professional Year in Australia.
  • Partner skills.
  • State or territory nomination (where applicable).

Applicants should ensure every point claim can be supported with valid evidence when lodging their visa application. Unsupported claims may affect the outcome of the application.

Understanding Your Competitive Score

Although being above the threshold is vital, there is a lot of competition in the invitation rounds. The level of occupation demand, state nomination requirements, and number of slots available may affect the cut-off score for getting an invitation. Keeping yourself updated about the state nominations will help you in this process.

State Nomination vs Family Sponsorship

The subclass 491 visa can be obtained through one of two routes. The first route involves being nominated by the state or territory government of Australia, while the second route involves being sponsored by a suitable relative who resides in a designated regional area of Australia. While both routes result in the same visa, their eligibility criteria and application process are different.

Which Pathway Should You Choose?

If you already have a close family member living in an eligible regional area, family sponsorship may be an appropriate option. Otherwise, state or territory nomination is often the preferred pathway for skilled professionals who wish to immigrate to Australia based on their occupation and skills.

Designated Regional Areas in Australia

Regional Australia includes all areas excluding the metropolitan areas of Sydney, Melbourne, and Brisbane. Living in these places will enable those people with a 491 visa subclass to contribute to the economy of these places, while also living a good lifestyle with increasing employment opportunities for them. The regional areas of Australia that qualify for this purpose have been decided by the government of Australia.

New South Wales (Regional)

Regional New South Wales offers opportunities in sectors such as healthcare, engineering, education, agriculture, and construction. Cities including Newcastle, Wollongong, Albury, and Wagga Wagga continue to attract skilled professionals.

Victoria (Regional)

Regional Victoria combines strong employment prospects with quality education and healthcare services. Areas such as Geelong, Ballarat, Bendigo, and Shepparton frequently attract skilled migrants.

Queensland (Regional)

Regional Queensland provides opportunities in mining, healthcare, tourism, engineering, agriculture, and construction. Popular destinations include Townsville, Cairns, Toowoomba, and the Sunshine Coast.

South Australia

South Australia regularly nominates skilled professionals across various industries depending on labour market needs. Adelaide and many surrounding regions are considered designated regional areas for the Subclass 491 visa. State nomination priorities and invitation rounds are updated periodically.

Western Australia

Western Australia offers opportunities across mining, engineering, healthcare, information technology, and skilled trades. Regional centres continue to seek qualified professionals to support economic growth.

Tasmania

Tasmania is a popular destination for applicants seeking a balanced lifestyle and employment opportunities in healthcare, education, hospitality, agriculture, and information technology.

Northern Territory

The Northern Territory actively supports skilled migration to address workforce shortages across healthcare, engineering, construction, education, hospitality, and regional services.

Australian Capital Territory (ACT)

While Canberra is Australia's capital city, it is classified as a designated regional area for the Subclass 491 visa. The ACT regularly publishes nomination criteria for eligible applicants.

Australia 491 Visa Occupation List

One of the essential criteria for the 491 visa class is that your nominated occupation should be listed under a relevant skilled occupation list. Depending upon whether you apply through state or territory nomination or eligible family sponsorship, there will be different lists for you. Every occupation is associated with an authorized skills assessing body.

Popular Occupations

Common occupations nominated under the skilled migration program include:

  • Software Engineer.
  • ICT Business Analyst.
  • Civil Engineer.
  • Mechanical Engineer.
  • Registered Nurse.
  • Medical Laboratory Scientist.
  • Accountant.
  • External Auditor.
  • Secondary School Teacher.
  • Early Childhood Teacher.
  • Electrician.
  • Carpenter.
  • Chef.
  • Motor Mechanic.
  • Construction Project Manager.

Eligibility for a specific occupation depends on the current skilled occupation lists and the nomination requirements of individual states and territories.

Skills Assessment Authorities

Every nominated occupation is assessed by an approved assessing authority.

Examples include:

  • Engineers Australia.
  • Australian Computer Society (ACS).
  • VETASSESS.
  • Trades Recognition Australia (TRA).
  • Australian Nursing and Midwifery Accreditation Council (ANMAC).
  • CPA Australia and other approved accounting bodies.

The correct assessing authority depends on your nominated occupation. A positive skills assessment is generally required before you can receive an invitation to apply.

High-Demand Industries

Although occupation demand changes over time, skilled workers are often sought in areas such as:

  • Healthcare
  • Information Technology
  • Engineering
  • Education
  • Construction
  • Renewable Energy
  • Agriculture
  • Advanced Manufacturing
  • Skilled Trades

Applicants should review current state nomination priorities before deciding where to apply, as these may differ between jurisdictions.

Preparing complete and accurate documentation is essential for a smooth visa application. Missing or inconsistent information may delay processing or affect the outcome of your application.

Australia Subclass 491 Visa Application Process

The process of applying for the subclass 491 visa is comprised of different steps, ranging from determining one's eligibility all the way to the decision about the visa. The careful planning of each stage of the process will make it easier for you to get the visa without encountering any issues.

At Visa For Nation, we assist our clients in going through all stages of the visa application process.

Step 1: Check Your Eligibility

Before beginning your application, confirm that you meet the basic requirements for the Subclass 491 Visa Australia, including:

  • Age requirement
  • Eligible occupation
  • Skills assessment
  • English language proficiency
  • Migration points
  • Health and character requirements

Understanding your eligibility early helps you choose the most suitable migration pathway.

Step 2: Select Your Nominated Occupation

Choose an occupation that appears on the relevant skilled occupation list and matches your qualifications and professional experience.

Selecting the correct occupation is important because it determines:

  • Your skills assessing authority.
  • State nomination opportunities.
  • Occupation-specific eligibility requirements.

Step 3: Obtain a Skills Assessment

You must receive a positive skills assessment from the approved assessing authority for your nominated occupation.

The assessment verifies that your education, qualifications, and work experience meet Australian standards.

Step 4: Demonstrate English Language Proficiency

Provide evidence of at least Competent English through an accepted English language test or another eligible pathway, where applicable.

A stronger English score may improve your migration points and strengthen your overall profile.

Step 5: Calculate Your Migration Points

Before submitting your Expression of Interest (EOI), calculate your migration points based on factors such as:

  • Age.
  • English language ability.
  • Skilled work experience.
  • Educational qualifications.
  • Partner skills (if applicable).
  • State nomination.

Although 65 points is the minimum eligibility threshold, higher scores may improve your chances of receiving an invitation because the process is competitive.

Step 6: Submit an Expression of Interest (EOI)

Create and submit your Expression of Interest (EOI) through SkillSelect.

Your EOI contains information about:

  • Personal details.
  • Skills assessment.
  • Employment history.
  • Education.
  • English language results.
  • Claimed migration points.

Submitting an EOI does not automatically result in a visa invitation.

Step 7: Apply for State Nomination (If Applicable)

If you are pursuing the state or territory nomination pathway, submit an application to the relevant state or territory government.

Each jurisdiction has its own:

  • Occupation priorities.
  • Nomination criteria.
  • Application procedures.
  • Invitation rounds.

Meeting the minimum visa requirements does not guarantee state nomination.

Step 8: Receive an Invitation to Apply

If your EOI is selected and you receive nomination or eligible family sponsorship, you may receive an invitation to lodge your visa application.

The information in your visa application must match the claims made in your EOI.

Step 9: Lodge Your Visa Application

After receiving an invitation, submit your complete visa application through your ImmiAccount within the specified timeframe.

Ensure all supporting documents are uploaded accurately, including:

  • Passport
  • Skills assessment
  • English language results
  • Educational qualifications
  • Employment evidence
  • Nomination documents
  • Police certificates
  • Medical examination reports (if requested)

Step 10: Complete Health and Character Checks

The Department of Home Affairs may request:

  • Medical examinations.
  • Police clearance certificates.
  • Additional supporting documents.

Responding promptly to requests can help avoid unnecessary delays.

Step 11: Receive the Visa Decision

After assessing your application, the Department of Home Affairs will notify you of its decision.

If granted, your visa grant notice will outline:

  • Visa validity
  • Visa conditions
  • Travel rights
  • Regional residence requirements

Australia Subclass 491 Visa Processing Time

The processing time for the subclass 491 visa varies depending on individual circumstances and government workload. There is no fixed timeframe for every application, and processing may differ based on factors such as document completeness, health and character checks, and the complexity of the case.

Factors that may influence processing include:

  • Complete and accurate documentation.
  • Timely responses to requests for additional information.
  • Health and character assessments.
  • Verification of employment or qualifications.
  • Annual migration program allocations.

For the most up-to-date estimate, applicants should use the Australian Government's official Visa Processing Time Guide, as timelines are updated regularly.

Can the Subclass 491 Visa Lead to Permanent Residency?

Yes. The subclass 491 visa will give a suitable pathway for permanent residency through the Subclass 191 Permanent Residence (Skilled Regional) visa.

It does not guarantee that you have met all the terms of your provisional visa; you will have to fulfill the required criteria that will be relevant when you apply for the subclass 191 visa.

Understanding the Subclass 191 Visa

The Subclass 191 Permanent Residence (Skilled Regional) Visa allows eligible holders of certain regional provisional visas, including the Subclass 491 visa, to live and work permanently in Australia.

Once granted, permanent residents may:

  • Live anywhere in Australia.
  • Work for any eligible employer.
  • Study without regional restrictions.
  • Sponsor eligible family members for permanent residence.
  • Apply for Australian citizenship if they later meet the citizenship requirements.

Eligibility for the PR Pathway

To be eligible for the Subclass 191 visa, applicants generally must:

  • Hold an eligible regional provisional visa for the required period.
  • Have complied with the conditions of that visa.
  • Provide Australian Taxation Office (ATO) notices of assessment for three income years within the five-year eligible visa period.
  • Meet health and character requirements.
  • Satisfy any other applicable legislative requirements at the time of application.

Planning Your Long-Term Migration Journey

An Application for the Subclass 491 Visa Australia may be only the beginning of the immigration process. Staying compliant with the visa requirements, keeping tax records properly, and being informed about the requirements for permanent residence will help you move towards the Subclass 191 visa easily.

At Visa For Nation, we assist our clients in planning their immigration journey from the point when they apply for the visa through to long-term migration, although all decisions regarding any visas are made by the Australian Government.

Common Reasons for Subclass 491 Visa Refusal

Being invited to apply for the visa does not ensure its approval. Each application is reviewed based on the existing migration laws and the evidence that is provided. Minor mistakes or lack of evidence can have an impact on the decision-making process.

Knowing the most frequent reasons for rejection allows making a better-prepared application.

Incorrect or Incomplete Documentation

Missing documents, inconsistent information, or incorrectly prepared evidence can delay processing or lead to refusal.

Common issues include:

  • Missing employment evidence
  • Incomplete education documents
  • Expired English language test results
  • Incorrect passport details
  • Missing civil documents

Always ensure every document supports the information declared in your application.

Invalid or Expired Skills Assessment

A valid positive skills assessment is an essential requirement for the Subclass 491 Visa Australia.

Applications may be affected if:

  • The assessment has expired.
  • The nominated occupation does not match your experience.
  • Supporting documents do not align with the assessment.

Unable to Prove Claimed Migration Points

When you submit an Expression of Interest (EOI), every claimed point must be supported with evidence.

Examples include:

  • Skilled work experience
  • Educational qualifications
  • English language results
  • Partner points
  • Professional Year
  • Community language qualification

If you cannot prove the points claimed in your EOI, your application may not meet the invited score.

Health or Character Requirements Not Met

Applicants and accompanying family members must satisfy Australia's health and character requirements.

This may include:

  • Medical examinations
  • Police clearance certificates
  • Additional background information if requested

Changes to State Nomination

For applicants applying through state or territory nomination, the nomination must remain valid at the time of visa decision. If the nomination is withdrawn, the visa cannot be granted.

Providing Incorrect or Misleading Information

Applicants should ensure every statement made in their EOI and visa application is accurate and supported by evidence.

Providing false or misleading information may affect the current application and future visa applications.

Tips to Improve Your Chances of Receiving an Invitation

Because the skilled migration program is competitive, improving your profile before submitting an EOI can increase your opportunities.

  • Improve Your English Score: Higher English language proficiency may increase your migration points and strengthen your overall profile.
  • Gain Additional Skilled Work Experience: More relevant skilled employment may improve your migration points, depending on your circumstances.
  • Choose the Correct Occupation: Select an occupation that accurately reflects your qualifications and experience and is listed on the relevant skilled occupation list.
  • Monitor State Nomination Programs: Each Australian state and territory has different nomination priorities and eligibility criteria.

faqs.q: What is the Subclass 491 Visa?
faqs.a: The subclass 491 visa is a points-tested provisional visa that allows eligible skilled workers to live, work, and study in designated regional areas of Australia after receiving state or territory nomination or sponsorship from an eligible relative.

faqs.q: Is the Subclass 491 Visa a permanent visa?
faqs.a: No. It is a provisional visa valid for up to five years. Eligible holders may later apply for the Subclass 191 Permanent Residence (Skilled Regional) Visa if they meet the applicable requirements.

faqs.q: Can I include my family?
faqs.a: Yes. Eligible family members may be included in your visa application if they satisfy the relevant requirements.

faqs.q: What is the minimum points requirement?
faqs.a: You generally need at least 65 migration points to be eligible. However, invitation scores may be higher depending on the occupation and nomination pathway.

faqs.q: Is state nomination compulsory?
faqs.a: Yes. Applicants must either receive a state or territory nomination or be sponsored by an eligible relative living in a designated regional area.

faqs.q: Can I work anywhere in Australia?
faqs.a: Subclass 491 visa holders are expected to live, work, and study in designated regional areas in accordance with their visa conditions.

faqs.q: Can I apply for permanent residency?
faqs.a: Yes. Eligible visa holders may apply for the Subclass 191 visa after meeting the legislative requirements, including holding an eligible regional visa and satisfying the applicable criteria at the time of application.

faqs.q: Do I need a migration consultant?
faqs.a: No. It is not mandatory. However, many applicants choose professional guidance to better understand eligibility requirements, documentation, and application procedures.
